verses.1: And Satan stood against Israel, and he tried to destroy David in order to destroy Israel.
verses.2: And David said to Joab and to the commanders of the army, “Go and count Israel from Seba to Dan. Then bring them to me, so that I can know their numbers.”
verses.3: And Joshua said to Josue, “May the LORD have mercy on His people. They have done this a hundred times. But why does my Lord demand this from them? Why should it be a reproach for Israel?”
verses.4: And the king’s words had an overwhelming effect on Joab. So Joab went out and traveled throughout all of Israel. Eventually, he arrived in Jerusalem.
verses.5: Joaab gave the number of people who were to be taken captive by David. In total, all of Israel numbered eight hundred thousand men who were to be taken captive. And Judah numbered four hundred and seventy thousand men who were to be taken captive.
verses.6: And Levil and Binyamun did not pay attention to them, because the king’s words had offended Yoav.
verses.7: And it became a disgrace in the eyes of God because of this act. And Israel was destroyed.
verses.8: And David said to the Lord, “My sins are too great. I have done this and that. Now, please let my servant die, for I am completely lost.”
verses.9: And the LORD spoke to the prophet David, saying:
verses.10: Go and tell David, “As the LORD has said, I will choose you from among your people. I will do this for you.”
verses.11: And Gad went to David and said to him, “As the Lord has said, you shall receive it.”
verses.12: If three years of famine and if three new plagues befall you because of your sins, and if your enemies destroy your crops. If for three days there is destruction in the land, and if Jehovah’s wrath breaks out throughout all the boundaries of Israel… Now, see what I will do with those who send me here.
verses.13: And David said to Gad: “Oh, how I suffer greatly! May it be in the hands of Jehovah, for His mercy is great. But not in the hands of man.”
verses.14: And the LORD caused disease to spread among the Israelites. Seventy thousand men died from this disease.
verses.15: And God sent an angel to Jerusalem to destroy it. While he was destroying it, Jehovah saw what he was doing and felt sorry for the evil that had been done. Then He said to the angel who was destroying: “Now, stretch out your hand.” And the angel of Jehovah stood at the gate of Ornain, the Jebusite.
verses.16: David raised his eyes and saw the glory of the LORD standing between the earth and the heavens. His spear was broken in his hand, and he directed it against Jerusalem. David and the elders were covered with clothes on their faces.
verses.17: And David said to the Lord, “Have I indeed sinned against you? I am the one who has sinned and done wrong. My enemies have done evil to me. What have these sheep done? Please do not let them harm me, my family, or your people.”
verses.18: And the LORD said to Gad, “Tell David that when he goes up to build the altar for the LORD in the city of Zorah, he shall do it.”
verses.19: And David spoke words that were spoken in the name of Jehovah.
verses.20: And Arnan sat down, and he saw the angel. His four sons were also with him. Arnan cut the wheat into pieces.
verses.21: David came to Arnon. He saw Arnon, and he bowed down to David. Then Arnon stepped out of the forest and bowed to David.
verses.22: And David said to Ornan, “Give me a place where I can build an altar for the LORD. You shall provide the gold needed for building it. Then the plague will be stopped from spreading among the people.”
verses.23: And Arnan said to David, “Go and do what is right in the eyes of the king. I have given you everything: the monkeys for food, and the goats for fodder. All of it has been given to you.”
verses.24: And King David said to Arnan, “I will not buy it with money. I will not take anything from you for the sake of God. Let us just leave it as it is.”
verses.25: David gave Arnan the place where gold weights were kept. The weight of each weight was six tons.
verses.26: And there, David built an altar for Jehovah. He offered sacrifices and offerings of incense. Then he called out to Jehovah, and Jehovah answered him with fire from heaven upon the altar.
verses.27: And the LORD said to the angel, “Set your throne over Nodamah.”
verses.28: On that day, David saw that Jehovah had answered him in the garden of Erec. He then worshiped there.
verses.29: And from the tabernacle of Jehovah, which Moses built on the shore, and from the altar that he made at that time in the land of Moab.
verses.30: And David could not go before him to pray to God, because he was afraid of the wrath of the LORD.
